The Competition

A contest of reasoned argument

The CAASS Essay Competition is an academic essay contest across four disciplines: political science, philosophy, international relations, and economics. The project brings together a series of lectures on academic essay writing led by the coach of Kazakhstan's national philosophy team, a webinar with the founder of a major student journal and public speaker from Duke University, and the review and analysis of submissions by students from leading European, Russian, and Central Asian universities.

Choose one

Prompts

Each question invites a reasoned argument for a position; there is no predetermined correct answer. Respond to exactly one.

Political Science

In some states, power hardly resembles institutional frameworks like constitutions. Are deviations from the formally established order an inescapable part of how political systems function, or a corruption of politics?

Philosophy

Language is not just a mode of communication, but also a way of comprehending the world. Do the limits of language define what can be known to us, or does human understanding transcend linguistic boundaries?

International Relations

World order has been governed both through formal extra-national institutions and through direct contact between states. Do international organisations and security protocols shape the balance of power more than bilateral state-to-state relations?

Economics

Economics presents itself as an objective science of resource allocation. Is it truly an impartial description of the world, or does every economic model contain subjective premises about how society ought to function?

Max 1,500 words · English · Chicago referencing · no AI permitted.

Evaluation Rubric

CriterionWhat we look forMax
Argumentation (thesis & reasoning)A clear thesis that directly answers the chosen question and commits to a position. Reasoning is logical and sustained; the strongest essays anticipate and answer the best objection to their own case.15
Depth of research (evidence)Claims are supported with relevant, accurate evidence: cases, data, texts, or examples appropriate to the discipline. A cited authority should do argumentative work, not serve as decoration.15
Structure & clarityCoherent organisation and logical flow from thesis to conclusion. Each paragraph advances the argument; transitions are clear; prose is precise and controlled.15
Language & citationsCorrect grammar, spelling, and register, with minimal mechanical errors. Complete and consistent Chicago-style referencing.10

Submission requirements

Length
Max 1,500 words, excluding footnotes and bibliography. Over-length entries may be penalised or disqualified.
File title
Respond to one prompt; title the file Name_Surname_Discipline (e.g. John_Doe_Economics).
Language
English.
Referencing
Chicago style, using the notes–bibliography system: a numbered footnote at each citation plus a full bibliography.
Format
Times New Roman, 12-point, double line spacing.
Use of AI
No AI is permitted at any stage. Detected use results in disqualification.
Originality
Entries must be the entrant's own unaided work. Plagiarism results in disqualification.
Eligibility
Secondary-school students aged 14–18. One essay per entrant.
Questions
Direct queries about these regulations to caass.edu@outlook.com.
Assessed by university students

Our Judges

Essays are evaluated by a broader judging panel composed of university students. Institutions include: Nazarbayev University, American University of Central Asia, Moscow State University, Moscow State Institute of International Relations, University of Milan, Corvinus University of Budapest, University of Birmingham, University of Reading, and University of Bristol.

For the winners

Awards

1

Essay debrief

Winners receive a personalised debrief on their essay from the competition's head judges, the coaches of Kazakhstan's national philosophy team.

2

Publication in Inspire Youth Journal

Winning essays are eligible for publication in Inspire Youth Journal, subject to the journal's peer-review process.

3

Website feature

The top ten essays will be published on the CAASS website.
